conflicts.point: Whether upstream pre-export controls and data provenance checks can effectively prevent safety risks without disabling open-source AI development.

positions.stance: Strict pre-export checks and audits are necessary to prevent unrecoverable safety failures caused by releasing frontier model weights.
Upstream controls are ineffective against peer-to-peer distribution and only serve to disadvantage open-source developers relative to entrenched labs.

conflicts.point: Whether the primary policy risk is catastrophic safety failure from uncontrolled model release or economic stagnation from monopolistic gatekeeping.

positions.stance: Public model weight release permanently ends human control, requiring society to prioritize risk containment above all else.
Regulatory delays cost human lives by slowing medical and scientific innovations, making permissionless abundance the overriding moral baseline.

verdicts.conflict: Whether upstream pre-export controls and data provenance checks can effectively prevent safety risks without disabling open-source AI development.
verdicts.rationale: Both sides present plausible structural dynamics but lack definitive empirical tests under current Export Control Reform Act frameworks. Accelerationists correctly identify bureaucratic capture risks, while skeptics accurately highlight the lack of data provenance visibility in current open releases.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal data tracking compliance costs for small developers versus large labs under recent Bureau of Industry and Security export rules.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the primary policy risk is catastrophic safety failure from uncontrolled model release or economic stagnation from monopolistic gatekeeping.
verdicts.rationale: This conflict reduces to an incommensurable trade-off between existential risk minimization and economic liberty. Safety advocates prioritize low-probability high-consequence outcomes, whereas accelerationists focus on immediate scientific utility and market competition.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Validated evaluation benchmarks that accurately quantify the dangerous capability threshold of open-weight models relative to closed systems.
